clue.text: A ship can somehow get into the river with confidence

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship

indicators.note: get into says the jumbled letters are placed inside the river's name

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a crossword favourite

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of the word can are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: A vessel's tin is mysteriously sunk in a river, done with complete self-assurance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ship can' looks like the boat's tin; 'can' is in fact the anagram fodder, with the adverb after it as its signal, and 'get into' is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Assurance is a synonym for self-belief or certainty, the sense of confidence here.

clue.text: Dog has a disgusting habit, it is reported

indicators.note: it is reported signals that the phrase before is to be taken as spoken, a homophone

parts.note: someone who spits has an unpleasant habit

explanation.surface: A dog is said to have an unpleasant habit.
explanation.definitionFit: The spitz is a breed type of dog with a pointed muzzle and curled tail.

clue.text: Not in good health during a French spring

parts.note: un is the French word for a
a well is a spring of water

explanation.surface: Someone falls ill while on holiday in France during spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' is only a link here; 'spring' looks like the season but is a water source.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwell is a plain synonym for poorly or sick.

clue.text: A large misuse of vinegar

indicators.note: misuse of says the letters of A large are put to wrong use, scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone is wasting a big quantity of vinegar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misuse of' rearranges the six letters of A LARGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Alegar is an old word for malt vinegar, literally sour ale.

clue.text: See or hear of snag

definitions.meaning: to ... something is to glimpse it or hear it, as in ... a remark

explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both perceiving something briefly and a hidden drawback in a deal.

clue.text: Not the talk of island dwellers, it is understood

definitions.text: Not the talk of island dwellers
definitions.meaning: playfully, the language of people living on plains rather than islands
speech that is clear and simple is understood by everyone

explanation.definitionFit: Plain speech is wording free of jargon, so it is easily grasped; whimsically it is also the tongue of flatland folk.

clue.text: Angelic voices?

parts.note: the singers in paradise, a company of angels, give angelic voices

explanation.definitionFit: The choir of angels in paradise is the source of angelic singing.

clue.text: Exhausted sportsman?

parts.note: all in means exhausted, and also names a free-style grappling sport, so the competitor in it is the sportsman

explanation.definitionFit: All-in is slang for exhausted and also a style of grappling, so its competitor is an all-in sportsman.

clue.text: I'd pass him crashing towards the centre of the vessel

definitions.text: towards the centre of the vessel

indicators.note: crashing suggests the letters of I'd pass him are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone warns that a passing boat will collide with them in the middle of the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashing' rearranges the nine letters of I'D PASS HIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Amidships is the nautical term for the middle part of a ship.

clue.text: Meaning to be popular giving patient attention

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
tending is caring for, as a nurse tends a sick person

explanation.surface: A nurse sets out to become well liked by caring for patients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patient' looks like an adjective for careful attention, but the reading is caring for a patient.
explanation.definitionFit: Intending is a synonym for planning or having in mind, the verb sense of meaning.

clue.text: Graduate in Zaire's capital, a port

parts.note: an MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate

indicators.note: capital here means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A university graduate is posted to the capital of Zaire, which is a port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' does not mean Kinshasa; it asks for the first letter of Zaire.
explanation.definitionFit: Mainz is a German city with a port on the Rhine.

clue.text: Some behave neurotically at the refuge

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people act anxiously in a shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across beHAVE Neurotically. 'at the' is part of the definition phrase, read loosely as a place of refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: A haven is a place of safety or shelter.

clue.text: Look daggers in regal fashion

indicators.note: in regal fashion says the word regal is shaped into a new form

explanation.surface: A monarch shoots a stern look, as royalty does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in regal fashion' looks like a manner of looking; 'fashion' is a verb sense, to rearrange REGAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To glare is to stare angrily, which is what looking daggers means.

clue.text: Information concerning a literary style

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone gives facts about a particular kind of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A genre is a category or kind of writing, such as crime or romance.

clue.text: Like some gardens that are crooked

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of
Kew Gardens are the famous botanic gardens in London

explanation.surface: Some gardens are laid out off the straight.
explanation.walkthrough: KEW is the Royal Botanic Gardens in west London, so 'Like some gardens' is AS KEW.
explanation.definitionFit: Askew means at an angle or not straight.

clue.text: Sideways in NE London according to a cockney

indicators.note: a cockney speaker famously drops the initial h sound of a word

parts.note: Hendon is a district of north London

explanation.surface: A Londoner from the north-east describes something as side-on.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class East Londoners, drop their H, so HENDON becomes ENDON; Hendon is strictly in north-west London.
explanation.definitionFit: End-on describes something seen or placed with its end facing, the opposite of side-on, loosely sideways.

clue.text: Pour on cold water to weaken the spirit

definitions.text: Pour on cold water to weaken the spirit

parts.words: Pour on cold water to weaken the spirit
parts.note: reads like discouraging someone, but literally means adding water to a strong drink such as whisky

explanation.definitionFit: Adding water to an alcoholic spirit thins it and lowers its strength.

clue.text: Subtle difference when one's leaving a troublesome thing

indicators.note: leaving says the letters for one's go away from the word before

parts.note: a nuisance is an annoying thing
one is I, and one's is read as I with S, or I is

explanation.surface: A small distinction appears once an annoying item has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' gives I plus S, which 'leaving' removes from NUISANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuance is a fine shade of meaning or a slight distinction.

clue.text: Not in gear

parts.note: gear is clothing, so being out of it means wearing nothing, not a car out of gear

explanation.definitionFit: Someone wearing no clothes at all is unclothed, with no gear on.

clue.text: To be performing in time deserves recognition

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: an hour is a period of time
an actor who is on is performing

explanation.surface: Playing on schedule earns an actor praise.
explanation.definitionFit: An honour is an award or mark of esteem given in acknowledgement.

clue.text: Approved of seeing girl's name in the dictionary

indicators.note: in says the name goes inside the dictionary

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
Kay is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Someone is pleased to find a girl's name listed in the dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: To OK something is to sanction or give approval to it.

clue.text: Man we'd moved in with

indicators.note: moved says the letters of we'd change position

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man moved in with us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved in with' reads like a house move; 'moved' is the anagram signal for the apostrophe-free letters of we'd, and 'with' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Edwin is a male first name.

clue.text: Gave particulars of an item

definitions.meaning: a single small part or point

explanation.walkthrough: The verb sense is present tense, so 'Gave' reads loosely; the clue probably read 'Give'.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means itemise specifics; as a noun it means one particular point.

clue.text: In the same place I am about to offer a direction

indicators.note: about says the first piece goes around what follows

parts.note: I'm is the short form of I am
to bid is to make an offer
E is east, a compass direction

explanation.surface: Someone is about to give directions to a place.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibidem is the Latin footnote term meaning in the same source or location.

clue.text: Cash enclosure

definitions.meaning: a pen for stray animals or impounded cars

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both British currency and a pen for strays or towed cars.

clue.text: Flower is seen in time

indicators.note: seen in says the next piece sits within the time word

parts.note: a day is a period of time

explanation.surface: A flower blooms when its season comes.
explanation.definitionFit: The daisy is a common white-petalled bloom.

clue.text: Wooden pale!

definitions.meaning: grey-white in the face, as with shock

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both made from a particular tree's timber and pallid with fear.

clue.text: Anything you say should

indicators.note: you say signals that the word is heard as spoken, a homophone

parts.note: ought means should

explanation.surface: Whatever you say should be done.
explanation.definitionFit: Aught is an old word meaning any part or anything at all.

clue.text: Commander elected twice? More than that

definitions.text: Commander elected twice? More than that

parts.words: Commander elected twice? More than that
parts.note: an Aga is a Turkish commander and in means elected, so the phrase repeats that pair with and between; more than twice means repeatedly

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means repeatedly, many times over, which is more than just twice.

clue.text: It is very sweet to ride around a pad

indicators.note: around says the riding word goes round the pieces that follow

parts.note: to cycle is to ride a bicycle
a mat is a pad, as a mouse mat

explanation.surface: Someone thinks it is lovely to cycle round a flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyclamate is an artificial sweetener many times sweeter than sugar.
